newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Japanese Emporer Akihito arrives in Brazil.
newsitem.headline: Japanese Emporer Akihito arrives in Brazil.

text.p: Japanese Emperor Akihito and Empress Michiko arrived in Brazil on Saturday at the start of a two-week official visit to South America which also includes Argentina, an official said.

The imperial couple landed in a private jet in Belem, a crumbling, colonial city at the mouth of the mighty Amazon River, shortly after 9 p.m. (0100 GMT) and went straight to a hotel to rest, the official said.
Akihito and Michiko were due to go on a boat trip on the Amazon on Sunday before meeting with local government officials and representatives of the Japanese community who live in the area.
Immigrants from Japan began arriving in Brazil at the turn of the century, attracted by the country's coffee boom, and now represent the biggest Japanese community outside Japan.
Japanese families started settling the Amazon in the 1920s. Since then, they and their descendents have established successful tropical fruit and black pepper farms in the jungle.

The imperial couple were due to fly to capital Brasilia on Monday for an audience with President Fernando Henrique Cardoso. They will also visit the cities of Belo Horizonte, Sao Paulo, Curitiba and Rio de Janeiro.

Akihito and Michiko were expected to be given a particularly warm welcome in Sao Paulo, home to most of the 1.3 million Brazilians of Japanese descent. Television newscasts on Saturday showed drummers dressed in colourful robes putting the final touches to a performance they will give the couple.

Despite the traditional reverence shown by the Japanese for their emperor, one woman said she might break with protocol. "If I can, I'll give him a kiss, and the empress too," the woman, a member of a female choir, told national Globo television.

As well as their historical links, Brazil and Japan are big trade partners with $6.5 billion of business done between the two countries in 1995. Japan also provides Brazil with technical and financial assistance for agricultural, energy and environmental projects.

The emperor and empress were due to fly to Buenos Aires June 9 for a three-day visit to Argentina. Throughout their trip, the emperor and empress will be protected by Japanese police rather than the imperial guards normally used on foreign visits.
The measure was seen as a sign of heightened security concerns in Japan following the four-month hostage drama at the Japanese ambassador's residence in Peru.
